lead: Bought non-alcoholic drinks and drinking water — bottled water, sodas, tonics and mixers, juices, syrups and cordials, fermented soft drinks, energy and sports drinks, and ready-to-drink coffee and tea — organised by drink type, then named styles, icons and makers; recipes live in the Culinary Taxonomy.

depts.note: Tier for everyday bottled water; variety for named mineral-water sources compared by enthusiasts.

b.v: table / purified water · spring water · natural mineral water
b.w: EU Directive 2009/54/EC and US FDA bottled-water definitions

b.v: TDS very low (<50 mg/L) · low · medium · high · rich in minerals (>1500 mg/L)
still · lightly sparkling · naturally sparkling · fully carbonated
b.w: label terms (naturally carbonated, with added CO2)

s.brief: Archetypes are named sources with their spring and country: Evian, Volvic, Vittel, Fiji, Voss, Highland Spring, Gerolsteiner (still), Contrex, Hildon. Record TDS / key minerals and source where the source page gives them. Tier list (market leaders and supermarket staples) for purified/table water. Types: bottle size, glass vs PET, carton/can.

k.brief: Dasani, Aquafina-style purified/remineralised water
high-pH, electrolyte-added, hydrogen and oxygenated waters; one kind with types
bagged ice and clear cocktail ice; kind-level, few or no models

s.brief: Archetypes: San Pellegrino, Perrier, Badoit, Gerolsteiner, Apollinaris, Ferrarelle, Topo Chico, Vichy Catalan, Borjomi, Mattoni, Saratoga. Distinguish naturally sparkling from added CO2. Flavoured seltzer icons: LaCroix, Bubly, Polar. Soda/club soda as a mixer belongs on the Mixers shelf.

k.brief: naturally sparkling and carbonated mineral waters

depts.note: Carbonated soft drinks by flavour family; regional icons are the collecting and comparison axis.

b.v: full sugar · cane sugar · reduced sugar · zero / diet
can · glass bottle · PET · fountain / syrup
b.w: enthusiast preference for glass-bottle and cane-sugar versions

s.brief: Archetype = flavour icon with originator and year: Coca-Cola (1886), Pepsi, Dr Pepper (pepper/spiced soda), 7 Up and Sprite (lemon-lime), Fanta and Orangina (orange), Mountain Dew (citrus), A&W and Barq's (root beer), cream soda, grape soda (Welch's/Fanta Grape). Versions: diet/zero, cherry/vanilla, Mexican cane-sugar Coke, regional bottlings. Craft colas (Fentimans, Fritz-Kola) as versions or archetypes. Diet/zero are types, not kinds.

k.brief: grape, strawberry, pineapple, tropical
British clear lemonade, limonata (San Pellegrino), French limonade

s.brief: Regional icons with originator, country and year: Irn-Bru (Scotland), Inca Kola (Peru), guaraná (Guaraná Antarctica, Brazil), Ramune (Japan), Vimto (UK), chinotto (Italy), Almdudler (Austria), Sinalco, Afri-Cola, Kola Champagne, sarsaparilla, Cheerwine, Moxie, Big Red, Tango, Ting, Jarritos (Mexico), Thums Up (India), Mirinda, Bundaberg. Group by flavour family; record country. Do not duplicate mainstream icons from the previous shelf.

k.brief: Irn-Bru, Inca Kola, kola champagne
chinotto, Sanbittèr-style non-alcoholic bitter aperitivo sodas
sarsaparilla, Almdudler, Moxie
Jarritos, Sidral Mundet, Postobón
Vimto, Ting, Tango and other heritage fruit sodas not covered elsewhere
small-batch craft sodas and modern prebiotic sodas (Olipop, Poppi)

depts.note: Premium mixers are compared like spirits; mainstream mixers are a tier choice.

b.v: light / slimline · Indian tonic · aromatic · craft
b.w: quinine content and sugar per label; mixer brand comparisons

s.brief: Archetypes: Schweppes Indian Tonic (originator of commercial tonic), Fever-Tree, Fentimans, Q Mixers, Thomas Henry, 1724, Franklin & Sons; ginger beer (Fentimans, Fever-Tree, Bundaberg, Old Jamaica) and ginger ale (Canada Dry, Schweppes). Versions: light, aromatic, Mediterranean, elderflower. Cocktail mixes (margarita, Bloody Mary, sour mix) as a tier list. Alcohol-free spirits stay in J7.

k.brief: margarita, Bloody Mary, sour and mojito mixes

depts.note: Pick a good one: juice content, processing and freshness matter more than brand.

b.v: juice drink · nectar (25–50%+) · juice from concentrate · not-from-concentrate · freshly squeezed
b.w: EU Fruit Juice Directive 2012/12/EU; US FDA labelling

b.v: ambient (UHT) · chilled pasteurised · HPP cold-pressed · freshly squeezed

s.brief: Tier lists: market-covering brands (Tropicana, Innocent, Minute Maid, Del Monte, Ocean Spray, Pago, Granini, Rauch) plus independent taste-test winners. Archetype-level only where a named style exists (e.g. Spanish/Italian blood orange, Bloody Mary-style tomato juice, Indian nimbu pani as bottled product). Coconut water, birch water and aloe drinks go on the Plant waters kind. Pulp, from-concentrate and organic are types.

k.brief: cloudy/clear and single-variety pressed apple juice as types
pineapple, mango, passion fruit, guava, pomegranate
HPP cold-pressed juices and ginger/wellness shots
coconut water, birch water, maple water, aloe vera drink, cactus water

depts.note: Tier for everyday squash; variety for café and cocktail syrups and regional cordial traditions.

s.brief: Archetypes: Robinsons and Ribena (UK squash and blackcurrant cordial), Rose's lime cordial, Belvoir and Bottlegreen elderflower cordial, Teisseire and Monin (French sirops), Torani (café syrup), grenadine, orgeat, Rooh Afza (sharbat), Sirop de Liège is a spread (exclude). Add a tradition entry for sharbat / sherbet cordials and for drinking vinegars/shrubs where sources allow. Powdered mixes: Tang, Kool-Aid, Tang-style. SodaStream concentrates as soda-maker syrup.

k.brief: grenadine, orgeat, falernum (non-alcoholic), simple syrup
liquid drops and tablets (MiO-style)

depts.note: Living or traditionally fermented non-alcoholic drinks; dairy kefir and drinking yoghurt are in J3.

s.brief: Archetypes and traditions with region: kombucha (originators and leading makers such as GT's, Remedy, Equinox), jun, water kefir (tibicos), kvass (Russia/Ukraine/Baltics), boza (Balkans/Turkey), tepache (Mexico), mauby (Caribbean), malta (non-alcoholic malt soda: Malta Goya, Supermalt), traditional brewed ginger beer, amazake (Japan), sikhye (Korea), chicha morada and switchel only if they are sold bottled. Add tradition entries (g: Food & drink) for kvass, boza, tepache, mauby.

k.brief: traditionally fermented, plant-based ginger beer (soft-drink strength)
amazake, sikhye, horchata as bottled products

depts.note: Tier for everyday use; energy-drink cans are also a collecting area.

b.v: caffeine mg per can · sugar g · zero sugar

s.brief: Archetypes: Krating Daeng (Thai originator) and Red Bull, Lipovitan (Japan), Monster, Rockstar, Celsius, Prime, Lucozade (energy and sport), Gatorade (originator of sports drink, 1965), Powerade, Pocari Sweat, BodyArmor; mate sodas such as Club-Mate. Versions: flavours/editions only when significant (e.g. Red Bull Sugarfree, Monster Ultra). Electrolyte tablets and powders (Liquid I.V., Nuun). Medical oral rehydration salts belong to H2.

k.brief: Club-Mate and other yerba-mate based sodas
ready-to-drink protein shakes and recovery drinks
vitamin waters, nootropic, adaptogen and relaxation drinks

depts.note: Bottled and canned coffee and tea; leaf, beans and capsules are in J6.

b.v: can · PET bottle · chilled carton · hot vending can

s.brief: Archetypes: UCC Coffee with Milk (1969, first canned coffee), Georgia, Boss, Starbucks Frappuccino bottled, Nescafé RTD, cold brew (Stumptown, La Colombe draft latte); Arizona and Lipton Ice Tea, Snapple, Pure Leaf, Fuze Tea; Japanese bottled green tea (Itoen Oi Ocha, Suntory Iyemon), barley tea (mugicha), oolong (Suntory), Hong Kong-style milk tea, Taiwanese milk tea / bubble tea kits, Guayakí yerba mate cans. Order by significance.
